depth.h2: What Mokena Homes Need From a Plumber
depth.intro: Mokena grew fast. The village had about 1,600 people in 1970 and more than 18,000 by 2010, and the median home here was built in 1995. That means thousands of homes with plumbing of about the same age, wearing out on about the same schedule.

tiles.title: Subdivisions Hitting the 25 to 30 Year Mark
tiles.body: More than half of Mokena’s homes were built between 1990 and 2009. The first water heater, the first sump pump and the first ejector pump in those homes were never meant to last 30 years. A [water heater that leaks or runs out too fast](/mokena/water-heater-repair) is usually the first to go, and a [whole-home checkup](/mokena/plumbing-maintenance) shows what’s next.

tiles.title: Flash Flooding and Basement Backups
tiles.body: In August 2025, the National Weather Service reported significant flash flooding in Mokena, as storms dropped 4 to 8 inches of rain across the region. Storms like that test every sump pump in town. A [sump pump with a battery backup](/mokena/sump-pumps) keeps running if the power goes out, and a [backflow valve](/mokena/flood-control-maintenance) stops sewer water from coming up through a floor drain.

tiles.title: Settled Sewer Lines and Roots
tiles.body: Newer PVC sewer lines don’t crack like old clay, but they can sag where the soil settled after the house went up. Water and debris collect in the low spot, and roots from trees planted with the subdivision find any loose joint. [Sewer rodding](/mokena/sewer-rodding) clears the line, and a [camera inspection](/mokena/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows whether it needs a [repair](/mokena/sewer-repair).

tiles.title: Winter Freezes and Outdoor Spigots
tiles.body: Mokena winters bring long stretches below freezing. Pipes in exterior walls, garages and outdoor spigot lines freeze first, and a split pipe often starts leaking inside a wall once it thaws. We can [find and fix the leak](/mokena/leak-repairs), and we’re on call 24/7 if a [pipe bursts](/mokena/burst-pipe-repair).

items.q: How much does a plumber cost in Mokena?
items.a: It depends on the job. The main factors are what’s wrong, how hard it is to reach, the parts or materials needed and the age of your plumbing. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins, so you know the cost going in. Give us a call and we’ll walk you through it.

items.q: How fast can you get to my home in an emergency?
items.preview: Call us any time, day or night, including weekends and holidays.
items.a: Call us any time, day or night, including weekends and holidays. Our Jodi Road office keeps our plumbers close to Mokena, and we [treat emergencies as a priority](/mokena/emergency-plumbing). Arrival times depend on the day, but we’ll get a plumber to you as soon as we can.

items.q: My home was built in the late 1990s. What should I check first?
items.preview: Start with the water heater, the sump pump and, if you have a basement bathroom, the ejector pump.
items.a: Start with the water heater, the sump pump and, if you have a basement bathroom, the ejector pump. Equipment that came with the house is often 25 years old or more by now. A whole-home checkup tells you what’s close to the end, so you can replace it on your schedule instead of after it fails.

items.q: What is power rodding, and does my sewer line need it?
items.preview: Power rodding is a motorized cable that cuts through roots and clogs in your main sewer line.
items.a: Power rodding is a motorized cable that cuts through roots and clogs in your main sewer line. If several drains are slow at once, or water comes up through the basement floor drain, the main line is likely blocked. We rod it clear and can [camera the line](/mokena/video-camera-sewer-inspections) to show you what caused it.

items.q: How do I keep my basement dry during heavy rain?
items.preview: Start with a sump pump in good shape, a battery backup in case the power goes out and a backflow valve on your sewer line.
items.a: Start with a sump pump in good shape, a battery backup in case the power goes out and a backflow valve on your sewer line. We can test your pump, check the discharge line and tell you which [flood protection](/mokena/basement-flooding) makes sense for your home.

items.q: When should I replace my water heater?
items.preview: Tank water heaters usually last somewhere around 8 to 12 years.
items.a: Tank water heaters usually last somewhere around 8 to 12 years. Rusty water, rumbling noises, a leak at the base or hot water that runs out faster than it used to all mean it’s time to have it checked. [Replacing it](/mokena/water-heater-installation) on your schedule is easier than dealing with a flooded basement.
